text.p: Canada's industry minister said on Thursday that Telesat Canada had been awarded one of Canada's direct broadcast satellite orbital positions.
"We've approved the Telesat proposal and licensed them to build and launch their satellite," Industry Minister John Manley said in a statement.

"By issuing this license, the government of Canada has put in place the elements required for a Canadian DBS solution, and we're now looking to the (direct-to-home television) industry to deliver first class services to Canadians."
Telesat is cooperating with part owner Spar Aerospace Ltd STZ.TO.
The companies plan to build and launch a high-powered 32-transponder DBS satellite into Canada's 91 degree WL orbital slot, Manley said.
Telesat Canada Ltd is 95 percent owned by Stentor, the telephone consortium led by BCE Inc unit Bell Canada, and five percent by Toronto-based Spar.
Telesat has said it plans to launch its DBS as soon as the fourth quarter of 1998.
The satellite will meet the foreseeable needs of Canada's DTH television industry, which has been constrained because of the lack of satellite capacity, Manley said.

Last month, AlphaStar Canada Inc was temporarily authorized to use U.S. satellite space to launch its direct-to-home broadcast service in Canada because there was not enough space available in Canada.
But once Telesat's satellite has been launched, there will be enough space for AlphaStar and the other Canadian companies aiming to supply DTH services in Canada, Telesat officials have said.
